question: A service stores each user's login session in the memory of the server that handled the login. What breaks when you add a second server behind a load balancer?
options: Users sent to the other server are logged out, because it has no session
explanation: Session data is stateful. The fix is a shared session store, so any server can read the session.

question: Some requests take 2 seconds and others take 20 ms. Which algorithm usually spreads the load more evenly?
options: Round robin, because it is the simplest
Least connections, because a busy server with slow requests has more open connections
Random placement, because it never fails
Send everything to the largest server
explanation: Least connections sends new work to the server that is least busy, so slow requests do not pile up on one server.

question: A health check only confirms that the server process is running. Why is that not enough?
options: It does not show whether the server can serve requests, for example when it cannot reach its database
Health checks must always be disabled
Process checks use too much memory
It is enough; no other check is needed
explanation: A server can be running but unable to do useful work. A useful health check tests the things the server needs to answer a request.
